transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... since my in-laws moved into our house, I’ve just been so keyed up and worn down all the time. It's affecting everything. I find myself snapping at my wife a lot, which isn't like me. 

And at work—I'm a manager for some artists—I've been avoiding calls I would normally just handle immediately. It actually got to the point recently where I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight. I just really need to figure out how to get back on track.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with family and friends?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean... I still want to do the things I usually enjoy, and I still care about seeing my friends. It's not that I've lost interest in any of it. It's just that I'm so wound up all the time lately that it's hard to actually relax when I do have some downtime. But the interest itself is definitely still there.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things, even when you know they might not happen, and does it feel hard to control that worry?

Not really. I mean, I'm definitely stressed about the situation at home with my in-laws, and that bleeds into my work, but I'm not sitting around worrying about random things that might never happen. It's more of a constant tension about what's actually going on right now, rather than an out-of-control worry about the future.
Have you found that things you normally enjoy don’t give you as much pleasure or satisfaction as they used to?

No, not exactly. Like I said before, I still want to do things, and when I actually manage to do them, I do still enjoy them. It's just that it's hard to get to that point because I'm so tense. But the actual enjoyment or pleasure I get from things hasn't really changed.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or feeling on edge even when there’s no immediate stressor present?

No, I don't really have any of that. My heart isn't racing, I'm not sweating or shaking... nothing like that. Like I said, I feel tense and on edge because of the situation at home, but it's not like my body is reacting that way out of nowhere. It's just a constant stress from what I'm dealing with.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel depressed. I'm just... I'm really stressed and frustrated about the situation at home. It gets to me, sure, but I'm not walking around feeling sad or down all day every day. It's just a lot of heavy pressure right now, not really a depression.
How long have you been feeling this way? Specifically, when did you first notice this constant tension and stress starting?
It's been... I'd say about a month now. That's when my in-laws moved into our home. The constant stress pretty much started right when they got there.
Have you experienced any traumatic event recently, or found yourself avoiding certain situations, having flashbacks, or being unusually alert as a result of something that happened?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been through any trauma... and I'm not having flashbacks or avoiding things, no. It's really just what I mentioned before. The tension is just from my in-laws moving in and being in the house all the time, not from some big traumatic event.
Have you had trouble sleeping or found yourself waking up in the middle of the night because your mind is racing about the situation at home?

No, my sleep is actually... it's fine. I don't really have trouble falling asleep, and I'm not waking up in the middle of the night with my mind racing. Once I get in bed, I usually just sleep straight through. The stress is really just during the day when everyone is actually awake and around.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or making decisions lately, even about things that you'd normally handle without a second thought?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with my concentration. Work is busy, but I'm managing my clients and making decisions just like I normally do. It's really just the constant tension at home that's getting to me, not my ability to focus.
